newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Thursday were quiet, with no sales following a brief but active burst of trading late Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
Bids Thursday at $67.00 were light and scattered and passed by owners asking $68.00, sources said.
Sales Wednesday totaled about 56,000 head in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 39,000 in Kansas, the sources said.
Fed cattle Wednesday sold at $68.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week.
Demand this week appeared to be mostly satisfied, with any sales expected to be clean-up trades, feedlot sources said.

Most of the top quality cattle that will likely grade select and choice reportedly were sold on Wednesday, which left a light number of "green" or unfinished cattle to be carried over next week, they said.
"I'm not worried about the carryover because they can use the extra days (on feed)," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
Fed cattle prices this week were pressured by lower beef prices following large cattle slaughter last week, they said.
